title: China Fired Stone Into Fake Jade at 1,300°C | China Travel Expert
description:
China fired plain stone into a glaze that looks like carved jade — at over 1,300°C.

This is Longquan celadon from Zhejiang. Its jade-green plum-green (梅子青) color comes from iron oxide in the glaze — not any dye — coaxed out by exact firing temperature and timing. In 2009 UNESCO added Longquan celadon's traditional firing technique to its Intangible Cultural Heritage list, the only ceramic firing technique on it.

🧭 Expert Tip: To watch it fired today, go to Longquan in southern Zhejiang, where family kilns still work — and pair it with the town's famous sword-forging workshops.
